title: Raising his daughter and the dangers of fear and permissiveness
summary: Cobb talks about his 22-year-old daughter, whom he raised after his wife's death, and about parental guidance.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Well, I really don't know. You know, because the way things have turned out today, you wonder.
I mean you wonder whether parents ...
Because they're too free and they do too much. Now I got one - 22 years old -- you saw her

She's pretty good for a girl. And I've been met mothers and fathers since of 14 years old when her the mother died. But I preach. I'm a man like this -- I keep the suggestion; I plant the seed and let it grow, but see, when you plant it, you

All right. But she's a pretty good girl for a girl of 22 years old. But I stay on top of it, and I'm proud of her, for her age, with all this going on here today. She's all right in my estimation, and she lives with me. Love her -- but I'm not gonna stop advising her. I can't. Any time I loosen up, no telling.
